faq: Which languages and package managers do you cover?
npm, yarn and pnpm for JavaScript, pip and Poetry for Python, Composer for PHP, Bundler for Ruby, and Gradle or Maven for Java. Tell us your stack in the form and we confirm before starting.
What if an update breaks something?
Each step is a separate commit, so we can undo one without losing the rest. If a package cannot be updated safely, we leave it, explain why and suggest an alternative.
Do you need tests to exist already?
It helps, but it is not required. Without tests we check the build, the main screens and key flows by hand on staging. We recommend adding a few tests first if the app has none.
Will you upgrade the framework itself?

Minor versions are in every package. Major framework upgrades, such as Rails, Laravel or Angular, are in the Standard and Premium packages, within the limits shown. Very large jumps may need a separate order.

desc:
Outdated libraries slow your team and leave known holes open. Ecom Swift LLC handles dependency and framework updates for your app: we audit what you use, update what is safe, test after each step and document what changed.

## What are dependency and framework updates?

Every modern app is built on packages written by other people: web frameworks, database drivers, UI libraries, build tools. A dependency update replaces an older version of one of those packages with a newer one. A framework update does the same for the main foundation of your app, which often means changes to your own code as well.

Updates come in three sizes. Patch updates fix small defects. Minor updates add features and should not break anything. Major updates can change how the package works, so your code may need to change with them.

## Why old dependencies become a problem

Packages are maintained by volunteers and companies who eventually stop supporting old versions. Once that happens, newly found vulnerabilities are no longer patched for you. Your app keeps running, so the risk stays invisible until something goes wrong or a customer sends a security questionnaire.

Delay also compounds. Skipping one major version is a small job. Skipping five means you must cross every breaking change at once, often with documentation that is hard to find. Teams that put updates off end up unable to install new tools, because those tools expect a newer base.

## How regular updates improve safety and speed of work

Current packages receive security fixes and bug fixes, so the same problems stop reappearing in your logs. They also tend to be faster and to support newer language features, which makes the code easier to write and read.

For your team, the gain is momentum. New developers can set the project up without strange workarounds. Build times and install steps become predictable. A clean lockfile means the version on a developer's machine is the version in production. Upgrades stop being a feared event and become routine maintenance.

## What a careful update pass includes

- An inventory of every direct and indirect dependency with its current and latest version.
- A list of known vulnerabilities and which ones apply to how you actually use the package.
- Minor and patch updates applied in small groups, with tests run after each group.
- Major upgrades done on a separate branch, one at a time.
- Fixes for breaking changes in your own code.
- Removal of packages nobody uses any more.
- A clean lockfile and a build that installs from scratch.
- Rollback notes, so any upgrade can be reversed quickly.
- Automated alerts for future updates.

## How we work

We start by reading your package files and build setup, then produce the audit. We agree with you which updates go in now and which wait. Each step is applied, built and tested before the next one starts, and risky steps live on their own branch so your main branch stays safe.

The Basic package covers minor and patch updates with a test run and a list of changes. Standard adds a set of major upgrades with fixes for breaking changes, a check on known vulnerabilities, a smoke test on staging and rollback notes. Premium adds more major upgrades, removal of unused packages, automated update alerts, lockfile clean-up and a roadmap for whatever remains.

If your project has few tests, we say so and add simple smoke checks around the areas we touch, so a broken update is noticed.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us a staging environment to test on.
- Tell us which packages are business critical.
- Keep your main branch stable while we work.
- Decide in advance who approves a risky upgrade.
- Schedule small updates regularly after this one.

**Avoid:**
- Updating everything in one commit.
- Ignoring a failing test to get an update through.
- Running a major upgrade straight on production.
- Deleting the lockfile to fix an error.
- Postponing a security patch because the app seems fine.

## Who this is for

This service suits a team whose app still runs an old framework version and fears touching it. It suits a founder whose customer asked for a security review and found outdated libraries. It also suits a company that wants its build working again after a long gap between releases.

## What we need from you

Access to your repository as a collaborator or developer user, a note on how to run the app and its tests, and a staging environment if you have one. We never need passwords, and nothing is changed outside your repository without your say.
